newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S growth will spur Canadian exports, study says.
newsitem.headline: U.S growth will spur Canadian exports, study says.

text.p: A vibrant U.S. economy will boost Canadian exports this year, while Canadian interest rates are expected to remain low, a report released on Tuesday by an economic research organization said.
The Conference Board of Canada said in its spring 1997 world outlook that Canada's trade outlook this year is bullish.

The Canada dollar also is expected to firm up when first-quarter data show a trade balance improvement, which will help the Bank of Canada successfully resist having to match interest rate rises by the U.S. Federal Reserve this year, the board predicted.
The forecasts assume continued strong growth in the United States.
"Booming U.S. growth is expected to spur Canadian exports, especially in the first half of the year," said Peter Hall, the board's senior research associate.
Overall, North America will come close to unseating the Asia Pacific region in economic growth, the board said.
Strong performances in all three North American economies will push regional growth to 3.0 percent in 1997, while the Asia Pacific region will grow at 3.3 percent, the board predicted.
